correctness.rationale: Every face uses at most two private petals, so the contractible central union of individual full C5 simplices decomposes the quotient into canonical two-petal summands. A complete nine-vertex R_3(C5 v C5) face enumeration produces exactly 134 nonempty faces; the explicit deterministic 66-pair matching has precisely critical faces bitmasks 1 and 390, and its reversed-Hasse directed graph on all 374 incidences is acyclic. This proves S^3, not only its homology. The sum/wedge argument proves the all-m count. Exact Lefschetz all-face traces +1,+1,-1,-1 establish integral generator signs for petal swap/reflections; natural quotient splitting yields the full signed unordered-pair module. Rational finite-group averaging determines quotient rational homology.

originality.rationale: The first full paper provides three-robust homotopy only for bipartite square sequences; a later all-connected-bipartite sphere-wedge classification still does not apply to an odd-five-cycle bouquet. Exact full published adjacent results on quadrilateral bouquets address different graphs and not this primitive C2^m semidirect S_m representation. The earlier bounded-independence paper concerns collapsibility. An ordinary three-cut complex is dual to a different disconnected-triple condition. Independent full base Morse and signed symmetry traces establish new scientific content under a named natural graph family. Search incompleteness remains a candid risk.

value.rationale: A natural nonbipartite one-vertex bouquet of odd pentagons is the first exact odd-petal structural counterpart to the recently classified bipartite robust-clique square sequences. The all-m homotopy decomposition and complete primitive integral wreath symmetry lattice are informative structural theorems, not an arbitrary finite census or a known-table recalculation. The reflection signs and marked contrast between S_m- and full-group invariants are not implied by nonequivariant Betti-number formulas.
